scope: Default values for the installer app's commissioning checklist: R32 domestic split and multi-split heat pumps (Daikin, Panasonic, Mitsubishi Electric), GB.

gradeLegend.M: manufacturer manual/guide/official page, via search-engine extract (not opened directly)
gradeLegend.O: legislation or scheme body document, via search-engine extract
gradeLegend.S: secondary (retailer, installer blog, trade press, council leaflet, job advert)
gradeLegend.C: computed (CoolProp 8.0.0 or arithmetic on sourced inputs)
gradeLegend.U: unverified recall or general trade practice; numeric U items are null with a 'candidate'

defaults.label: Strength/tightness test pressure

caveats: Live research was not possible: the workflow's shared web-search budget (200) was exhausted before this task, WebFetch failed DNS for every host, and shell egress to manufacturer, MCS, REFCOM, gov.uk and legislation.gov.uk hosts was refused. Re-run with web access (send a follow-up, or raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION) to verify.

Grade M/O/S figures were read from search-engine extracts gathered earlier today by other research agents in this workflow; nobody opened the underlying pages or PDFs. Spot-check against the PDF before relying on them.

Every core manufacturer test parameter (nitrogen test pressure and hold, vacuum target, decay test, flare torque) is null. The 'candidate' objects are the researcher's recall of the named manuals - NOT sources. Use them only as clearly labelled, editable placeholders that the F-gas tech lead confirms against each pilot model's installation manual before Pilot 1.
Never apply a test pressure above the outdoor unit's nameplate PS, whatever default the app shows.
Additional-charge rules are per outdoor model; several Mitsubishi rules are provisional and Daikin 2MXM50A8's chargeless length conflicts (10 m vs 20 m) in sources.
F-gas leak-check/record thresholds, certificate categories and approved company certification bodies (beyond REFCOM) are unverified; GB F-gas changes during 2025-2026 were not checked.
Electrical test limits (insulation resistance, RCD times, Zs) are recall of BS 7671/GN3 and unverified; the electrician's own EIC is the authority.

MCS 020(a) method details (background noise treatment, which sound power figure) were not verified; only the 42 dB(A) limit and the SI 2025/560 references are sourced. Whether air-to-air units fall within Class G was not confirmed from the legislation text.
No sourced labour durations or UK day rates were found; the labour block holds repo placeholders and low-confidence assumptions only.
Temperature-split acceptance windows have no manufacturer source; record them, do not fail jobs on them, until a per-model fleet baseline exists.
